content:
I have a command elaborator that is quite extensive (hundreds of lines of code). Almost all of my functions run in CoreM. In my top-level elab declaration I use liftCoreM to get into the CoreM monad, and I call my other functions from that point.

Unfortunately it seems I can't pretty-print terms from inside CoreM, because Lean.ppTerm requires a PPContext, which I can't get from CoreM. Meta.getPPContext would give me that context, and runs in MetaM. So I'm considering changing some or all of my functions to run in MetaM instead, so that I can pretty print.

However I can't see how to call a function in the MetaM monad from my top-level elab command. The book MetaProgramming in Lean 4 claims that CommandElabM extends MetaM, but from looking at the definition of CommandElabM that is not obviously true. If I try to invoke Lean.Meta.liftMetaM from my top-level elab command I get the error

failed to synthesize instance of type class
  MonadLiftT MetaM CommandElabM

So how can I get into MetaM from CommandElabM? Or is there some way to pretty-print a term from CoreM? Any advice is appreciated - thanks.
docs#Lean.Elab.Command.liftTermElabM (or docs#Lean.Elab.Command.runTermElabM, depending on what you want), and then you get down to MetaM automatically using the lift from MetaM to TermElabM.

Thanks for the helpful suggestion. I would not have thought of calling liftTermElabM, since I'm not actually elaborating any terms, only building a series of commands to elaborate.

Meanwhile, I've realized that a PPContext contains several fields, some of which I can get in CoreM, and I can specify {} for the others to say that I have no declared metavariables or local variables. Thus I can actually print a term in CoreM like this:

import Lean
open Lean

def fmt_term (t: Term) : CoreM Format := do
  let ctx : PPContext := {
    env := (← getEnv), mctx := {}, lctx := {}, opts := (← getOptions),
    currNamespace := (← getCurrNamespace), openDecls := (← getOpenDecls) }
  Lean.ppTerm ctx t

For my purposes this seems to work fine and will probably be the easiest approach.
